The plan is sound and correctly narrows the fix to default basetemp generation, but it should be more explicit about where sanitization is applied: target the `pytest-of-<user>` component only, after the existing user-resolution/fallback helper returns a string, so you don't accidentally affect unrelated path construction.

Add a concrete test expectation for the reported Windows-style username: if the raw username is `contoso\\john_doe`, assert the derived basetemp uses a single path component such as `pytest-of-contoso-john_doe` or `pytest-of-contoso_john_doe`, rather than only asserting generic success. That makes the regression guard sharper.

Prefer implementing sanitization as a small dedicated helper function with a focused unit-style test, instead of inlining replacements inside tempdir creation logic. This will make fallback-related tests easier to preserve and reduces the chance of missing `os.altsep` or platform-specific invalid characters.

One subtle case to include in the plan: usernames may contain characters beyond separators, such as `:` or `?`, even on non-Windows hosts when values come from environment variables. A parametrized test over a few representative bad usernames would improve coverage beyond the single backslash case.

Be careful with the replacement strategy so the result cannot become empty or degenerate (for example if the username is only invalid characters). The plan should mention falling back to a safe default token in that case to keep directory creation deterministic.
